feature: Gauntlet escrow and end-of-run storage distribution
status: five generated UI explorations saved; no gameplay code changed
scope: Hold common drops from every instance creature until completion
Announce rare drops to the whole party
Review distribution at completion and deliver directly into recipient storage
design_assumptions: Rares remain reserved for end-of-run distribution after announcement
Party names, loot quantities, rare assignments, approval and draft/vote rules are illustrative option details
Early exit, failed run, eligibility, disconnect and storage capacity behavior require implementation design

options.title: Party ledger
options.mechanism: The party leader edits an allocation table and reviews storage deliveries.
options.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: one high fidelity desktop fantasy MMORPG game UI proposal for Rabbit Lands.
Generate ONE standalone wide landscape 16:9 screen, high resolution, flat frontal view. The interface must be large, genuinely readable, implementable and visually polished, not a painterly illustration of a screen.
Game identity and visual language: Rabbit Lands; established classic desktop RPG interface with nearly black blue-green panels (#05090a), fine muted bronze/amber borders (#896234), warm ivory/gold text (#e9bd83), restrained cyan selection (#7cc6d4). Small chunky hand-painted matte fantasy item icons, sober functional buttons, broad clear forms. Tasteful bronze corner detailing only. Clean readable sans serif UI text with modest serif title. Subtle darkened Amberwood forest path and reward chest behind the modal; game scenery stays peripheral and dim. UI fills about 90 percent of the canvas. No browser chrome, device mockup, giant logo, modern SaaS styling, ornate clutter, illegible filler, watermark or comparison collage.
Scenario: gauntlet "The Resin Road" just completed by four sample party members Alder, Mira, Rook, Tamsin. All common drops from ALL creatures have accumulated in shared escrow until the run ends. Rare drops have already been announced to the whole party, remain visible in the pool, and get allocated during end-of-run distribution. Assigned loot goes directly into each recipient's personal storage.
Use the same illustrative pool in this option: Gold Coins 480; Wolf Fur 40; Bones 24; Raw Meat 16; Portal Shard 1 (RARE); Slouch Boots 1 (RARE). Equal common share for each player, where shown, is 120 coins, 10 fur, 6 bones, 4 meat. Keep arithmetic coherent. Rarity is communicated by both a label and an icon outline, not color alone. Sample rare assignments may vary by option.
Visible persistent slim announcement strip above the modal: "RARE FOUND: Portal Shard" and secondary "Party notified · Held for distribution".
Modal title: "GAUNTLET COMPLETE"; subtitle "The Resin Road"; supporting line "All creature drops held until completion".
Show clear recipients, assignment state, storage destination, and a deliberate final confirmation control. Do not make collected loot disappear on close. Subtle footer "Unsent items remain in escrow." Use only a modest amount of concise real interface copy. All labels must be well spelled, high contrast, and readable at a glance.

OPTION 01: PARTY LEDGER. A compact, practical shared allocation ledger, closest to the existing game's classic storage windows. Header small "01 · PARTY LEDGER".
Main layout: left 68 percent is a six-row table with item icon/name, Total, Recipient, Quantity; each common row shows a small "Split evenly" control, with 4 recipients represented by clear chips or avatars; each rare row has a dropdown-like recipient control. Set Portal Shard to Mira, Slouch Boots to Rook. A visible row highlights Portal Shard cyan with RARE tag. Small toolbar "Split common equally" and "Clear assignments". Main right 32 percent is "Storage deliveries" with four concise recipient cards, common-share count and rare bonus. All 4 cards show storage checkmark "Ready". Below table "6 of 6 item types assigned". Footer secondary "Save & close", primary button "CONFIRM & SEND TO STORAGE". The screenshot must convey editing a shared table plus a transparent per-player delivery preview. Retain plentiful breathing room, precise aligned columns and clear quantities.
options.review: Readable totals, equal common shares, explicit rare recipients and direct storage confirmation. Accepted as an exploration.

OPTION 02: PLAYER TRAYS. A visual drag-and-drop distribution board. Header small "02 · PLAYER TRAYS".
Different structure from a table: a wide top horizontal "Shared loot" tray has the six pool stacks as large inventory cards with icons and quantity badges. Under it a narrow row contains "Split common equally" and a quiet "Drag stacks to a player". Main body has FOUR equally sized vertical player storage trays side by side, one per Alder, Mira, Rook, Tamsin. Each tray has a portrait medallion, name, "Personal storage", a compact 2x3 item grid and delivery readiness. The equal common stacks are visibly staged in each player's tray. Portal Shard is shown as a dragged card hovering over Mira's tray, with a clear cyan drop target and a cursor; Slouch Boots already staged under Rook. Shared tray rare cards visibly show "Assigned" or "Being assigned" instead of implying duplicate extra items. Bottom status "Preview allocations before sending"; footer small "Unsent items remain in escrow.", primary "CONFIRM & SEND TO STORAGE". Make the drag action and four recipient destinations immediately obvious. Strong item icon readability, restrained bronze grid, no ornamental parchment.
options.review: Useful exploration: shared pool, four trays and drag target read clearly. Tamsin's waiting-for-rare label incorrectly implies every member must receive a rare; change to common-share-ready when implementing. Portraits are illustrative.

OPTION 03: PARTY VOTE. A cooperative rare-loot decision screen, with a horizontal step bar "1 Common shares" "2 Rare choices" "3 Send to storage"; step 2 active. Header small "03 · PARTY VOTE".
Left quarter: "Common loot" summary lists the four common totals and shows a completed check "Split equally", then "Each player: 120 coins · 10 fur · 6 bones · 4 meat". Main center: a large Portal Shard item card with icon, RARE badge and short "Choose your preference". Three distinct buttons "NEED", "GREED", "PASS"; below a four-row party vote list showing Alder: Pass; Mira: Need; Rook: Greed; Tamsin: Greed; every member has a completed check. A compact outcome box reads "Awarded to Mira" and "Need takes priority; ties are rolled". Adjacent smaller card shows Slouch Boots, RARE, "Awarded to Rook" with resolved icon. Right quarter: "Storage preview" four recipient summaries, rare destination arrows and 4/4 ready. Footer primary "CONFIRM & SEND TO STORAGE", secondary "Review common shares". Include a small discreet note "Example rule: Need / Greed / Pass". This is the end-of-run screen, not a combat popup. Clear hierarchy and legible large controls.
options.review: Readable common shares, Need/Greed/Pass choices, resolved rare recipients and storage preview. Vote rule is an illustrative option.

options.mechanism: Players choose rare items in visible turn order while commons split equally.

OPTION 04: PICK IN TURNS. A turn-based shared loot draft screen. Header small "04 · PICK IN TURNS".
At the top of the modal a prominent four-medallion horizontal turn queue names Mira first with cyan "CHOOSING", Rook second "NEXT", Alder third, Tamsin fourth. Under queue small "Rares are picked in turn · Common loot is split equally". Main center-left is a generous inventory display containing two large rare cards: Portal Shard selected, Slouch Boots available. A clear selection detail pane shows Portal Shard icon, RARE, "Mira's choice", button "CONFIRM PICK". Lower left compact "Common share per player" showing the exact 120 coins / 10 fur / 6 bones / 4 meat with four icons. Right third "Party storage preview" shows each player, their common share and blank rare slot, Mira preview Portal Shard, status "Awaiting pick". Under the queue a discrete turn navigation says "Round 1 · Pick 1 of 2" without a timer. Bottom final send button "SEND ALL TO STORAGE" is clearly disabled until "Finish rare picks to send". Secondary "Save & close"; footer "Unsent items remain in escrow." Small "Example turn order" label so no economy rule appears immutable. The core visual must communicate personal turn, remaining rare pool and final direct storage delivery.
options.review: Useful exploration: turn queue, rare pool and disabled final send convey the flow. Mira's name in the first storage-preview row contains generated lettering distortion. Turn order and portraits are illustrative.

options.title: Suggested split
options.mechanism: Review an editable suggested allocation, resolve rares, then approve the storage transfer.

OPTION 05: SUGGESTED SPLIT. The calmest, fastest end-of-run review UI, built around an editable suggested allocation. Header small "05 · SUGGESTED SPLIT".
Top status: "Common loot split equally" with green check, and a small action "Adjust split".
Main content: a TWO BY TWO grid of spacious recipient cards for Alder, Mira, Rook, Tamsin. Each has modest portrait, personal storage label, four common item icons with exact per-player quantities 120 / 10 / 6 / 4. Mira card additionally has Portal Shard rare icon; Rook card additionally Slouch Boots rare icon. Thin cyan destination arrows or small chest icons show that each goes to storage. Every card has a subtle "Edit" action and "Storage ready" check.
A horizontal RARE ITEMS review strip below cards lists "Portal Shard → Mira" and "Slouch Boots → Rook", small "Change recipient" controls, and "Suggested recipients · Review before sending". Lower compact shared total row shows all original pool totals, with status "All items assigned". Four small approval indicators read "Alder ready", "Mira ready", "Rook ready", "Tamsin ready". Footer secondary "Save & close", strong primary "APPROVE & SEND TO STORAGE". Above primary short "Each share goes directly to personal storage." The screenshot must communicate one clear review followed by a deliberate delivery confirmation, with uncommon clarity, moderate density and a credible classic fantasy game interface.
options.review: Clear equal common shares, editable rare recipients, per-player storage destinations and final approval. Suggested rare assignments are illustrative.

visual_review: All five generated images visually inspected. Pass means suitable for UI discussion, not production-ready runtime artwork.
